To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stability of milk protein stabilized oil-in-water emulsion droplets to calcium was enhanced by lactoferrin through the formation of lactoferin-milk protein complexes at the interface.

lactoferrin can form interfacial complexes with caseinate or wheyl protein at the interface of oil-in-water emulsion droplets, which can stabilize the emulsion in the presence of high Ca(2+) concentrations.
the stability of emulsion droplets stabilized by milk proteins can be enhanced by addition of a small amount of lacto ferrin at the interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel emulsion formulations based on the use of the interfacially active protein-lactoferrin to stabilize milk protein-coated oil-in-water emulsion in the presence of multivalent ions.
the formation of interfacial complexes between lactoferrin and caseins/whey protein and its potential to enhance calcium stability of oil-in-water emulsion.
the formation of the interfacially associated protein complexes and its potential to stabilize oil-in water emulsions against Ca(2+).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lactoferrin can be used as a potential stabilizer to improve the calcium stability of emulsified systems.
addition of small amount of lactoferin on the interface of emulsion droplets can largely enhance the stability of the milk proteins-coated oil droplets to calcium.
the addition of lactofferin can improve the calcium stability of emulsification systems stabilized by caseinate and WPI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interfacial complexation of the lactoferrin and milk proteins at the oil/water interface of emulsion droplets can effectively prevent the flocculation of the emulsion caused by calcium binding and reduce the electrostatic repulsive force between emulsion droplets, thus resulting in the enhanced emulsion stability in the presence of high calcium.
lactoferrin is a promising emulsifying and stabilizing protein for food emulsions and can be applied to improve the stability of emulsion droplets against Ca(2+).
the interfacial complexation between lactoferrin and caseins or whey proteins at the interface of emulsion droplets can effectively stabilize the emulsion against calcium destabilization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small amount of lactoprotein can significantly enhance the stability of milk protein-coated emulsion against Ca(2+) destabilization.
the stability of milk protein-stabilized oil-in-water emulsion against calcium can be enhanced by addition of a small amount of lactiferrin.
a small amount of lactotransferrin can improve the stability of emulsion droplets coated by milk protein in the presence of divalent ions.
